question: What is the primary physiological advantage of administering medication via the inhalation route?

options.A: Slowing down the systemic metabolism of active drugs
options.B: Ensuring 100 percent absorption into the bloodstream
options.C: Completely avoiding first-pass metabolism in the kidneys
options.D: Achieving rapid local action with a lower overall dose

explanation: Direct delivery to the target organ allows smaller drug doses to take effect quickly while reducing widespread systemic exposure. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is aerosol particle size a critical factor in successful inhalation therapy?

options.A: Larger particles are needed to stimulate alveolar gas exchange
options.B: Medium-sized particles between 1 and 5 micrometers reach the lower airways
options.C: Extremely small particles settle rapidly in the oral cavity
options.D: Particle size only affects the speed of systemic clearance

explanation: Particles within this specific micron range bypass upper airway barriers to deposit effectively in the bronchioles and alveoli. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which anatomical structure acts as the primary site of absorption for therapeutic aerosols reaching the deep lung?
explanation: The vast surface area and thin membrane of the alveoli facilitate rapid diffusion of medications into the pulmonary capillary bed. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What causes inhaled drug particles to deposit prematurely in the upper respiratory tract?

options.A: Rapid enzymatic breakdown of the drug by saliva
options.B: High airflow velocity causing inertial impaction at branching points
options.C: Excessive humidification within the oral cavity
options.D: Negative pressure generated during a normal expiration

explanation: Inertial impaction occurs when fast-moving particles cannot negotiate sharp turns in the upper airways and collide with the mucosal walls. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main functional difference between a metered-dose inhaler and a dry powder inhaler?

options.A: MDIs require no hand coordination, unlike standard DPIs
options.B: MDIs can only be used with an external air compressor
options.C: DPIs deliver liquid mists, while MDIs deliver solid crystals
options.D: DPIs rely on patient inspiratory force, whereas MDIs use a chemical propellant

explanation: Metered-dose inhalers utilize chemical propellants to aerosolize the drug, while dry powder inhalers depend entirely on the patient's forceful inhalation to draw the powder out. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: A patient with severe arthritis struggles to coordinate pressing a metered-dose inhaler while inhaling. Which equipment addition is most appropriate?

options.A: A spacer or valved holding chamber
options.B: An ultrasonic nebulizer with a nasal cannula
options.C: A dry powder inhaler with high resistance

explanation: Spacers trap the aerosol cloud, removing the need for precise synchronization between device actuation and inhalation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which drug category is most frequently indicated for rapid relief of acute bronchospasm?
explanation: Short-acting beta-2 agonists quickly relax bronchial smooth muscle, providing immediate reversal of acute bronchospasm. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering an inhaled corticosteroid in chronic asthma management?

options.A: To immediately dilate severely constricted bronchiolar passages
options.B: To suppress chronic airway inflammation and reduce hyperreactivity
options.C: To dissolve thick mucus plugs blocking the alveolar ducts
options.D: To stimulate rapid central nervous system respiratory drive

explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids act locally over time to reduce mucosal inflammation and prevent recurrent asthma exacerbations. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why is baseline lung auscultation a mandatory component of pre-administration assessment?

options.A: To determine the precise volume of air entering each alveolus
options.B: To confirm the absence of any foreign body obstruction in the trachea
options.C: To measure the exact oxygen saturation of pulmonary capillary blood
options.D: To provide a clinical reference point for evaluating post-treatment effectiveness

explanation: Auscultating before and after treatment allows the nurse to determine if breath sounds have improved, such as the clearing of wheezes. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient admitted with a severe asthma attack is drowsy, tachypneic, and unable to hold an inhaler steady. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Coach the patient through using a dry powder inhaler forcefully
options.B: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for ten seconds after actuation
options.C: Delay the treatment until the patient is fully alert and cooperative
options.D: Set up a continuous or intermittent face-mask nebulizer treatment

explanation: Nebulizers require minimal patient coordination and passive tidal breathing, making them ideal for distressed or uncooperative patients. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the recommended breath-hold duration immediately after inhaling an MDI dose?
explanation: A 10-second breath hold gives suspended aerosol particles time to settle onto the walls of the small airways and alveoli via gravity. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why must a nurse instruct a patient to wait approximately one minute between successive puffs of an MDI?

options.A: To allow the respiratory rate to return to baseline resting levels
options.B: To allow the propellant to reset and ensure the second dose reaches deeper airways
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing acute carbon dioxide retention
options.D: To ensure the canister has cooled down from the freezing propellant

explanation: Waiting between puffs allows the metering valve to refill and ensures the second dose penetrates effectively rather than bouncing off un-reset mechanisms. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: What nursing instruction prevents oral candidiasis in patients using inhaled corticosteroids?

options.A: Drink a full glass of acidic fruit juice right after treatment
options.B: Brush the teeth immediately with a strong antiseptic mouthwash
options.C: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with water and spit it out after use
options.D: Swallow the residual saliva immediately following inhalation

explanation: Rinsing removes residual steroid particles from the oral mucosa, preventing fungal overgrowth and hoarseness. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which clinical sign should a nurse monitor for in a patient receiving high-dose short-acting beta-agonist nebulization?
explanation: Systemic absorption of beta-agonists commonly stimulates beta-1 cardiac receptors and skeletal muscle receptors, causing increased heart rate and tremors. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why should spacer devices be allowed to air-dry rather than being dried with a towel?

options.A: Air drying is the only method that sterilizes the inside chamber completely
options.B: Fabric fibers from towels can dissolve into the plastic and block the valve
options.C: Towel drying generates static electricity that causes powder or droplets to stick to the walls
options.D: Towel drying cracks the plastic casing and ruins the metering seal

explanation: Static charge attracts medication particles to the sides of the spacer, significantly reducing the dose delivered to the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of home care education for a patient using an inhaler?

options.A: Checking the expiration date and storing the canister in direct sunlight
options.B: Monitoring the built-in dose counter to track remaining medication
options.C: Recognizing signs of a failing therapeutic response or worsening cough
options.D: Washing removable plastic components regularly with warm soapy water

explanation: Canisters should never be stored in direct sunlight or extreme heat, as pressurized containers can rupture. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)
